A productive nucleus is identified by what its formation does to later development, measured against a comparator, not by its size, age, persistence or resemblance to the finished form. A separates it from a structural seed (an early recognizable substructure) and from a kinetic nucleus (a state whose crossing changes later progression, possibly toward the wrong structure). Its measure is the interventional difference Δ_N = Pr(τ_F ≤ T \| do(I_N), c) − Pr(τ_F ≤ T \| do(I_0), c). The committor q(s) = Pr_s(τ_F < τ_K) ranks intermediates by their futures but does not by itself show causation. It bears on [QUESTION-038](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-038.md) and [QUESTION-380](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-380.md), and qualifies [CLAIM-185](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-185.md)'s anchor.
